Through the unique perspective of a thirteen-year-old girl on an all-gay cruise with her dying father in the late 1990s, the story offers the reader deep cultural insights and a poignant exploration of human nature. Specifically, it illuminates the concept of "chosen family"—as explicitly highlighted by the father showing his daughter "how people take care of one another when they aren't related by blood"—and illustrates how marginalized communities facing immense tragedy (the AIDS crisis) use fierce joy, humor, and solidarity as mechanisms for survival and comfort.
